🤖 THREEHALVES — THE CENTAUR ROBOT Threehalves is a 7-foot-tall teleoperated robot developed by Satyress. Its design combines a human-like torso and arms with a powerful four-legged chassis, creating a mechanical centaur built for environments that are too dangerous for humans. The idea behind Threehalves is simple: instead of sending a person into extreme heat, unstable terrain, darkness, hazardous industrial environments or disaster zones, a skilled operator can control the robot remotely and perform the work from a safer location. Unlike many humanoid robots, Threehalves is designed around tools and equipment that humans already use. Its modular limbs and quick-connect system allow it to be adapted for different tasks, while its four-legged platform provides stability on difficult terrain. The most unsettling part is probably its appearance. With its enormous size, humanoid body, four mechanical legs and distinctive horned head, Threehalves looks less like a traditional industrial machine and more like something from a science-fiction horror movie. But behind the terrifying design is a serious engineering concept: putting the machine in danger instead of the human. Threehalves is still a developing robotics project, but it represents a strange glimpse into a future where dangerous jobs could be performed remotely — with a human controlling the machine from a distance. And honestly… it might be one of the creepiest robots ever built. 👁️ #threehalves #robot #baal #satyress #horrortok

I spent days teaching a 3D-printed robot duck to walk. Most of that time, it was falling over. It’s my own build of the Open Duck Mini. The open-source, BDX-inspired biped created by Antoine Pirrone. The whole thing is 3D-printed and runs on hobby-grade servos instead of industrial actuators, which is what makes it buildable on a normal budget and also what makes it so hard to get walking. The hard part wasn’t the printing or the assembly. It was the sim-to-real gap. A gait that walks perfectly in MuJoCo hits real-world joint slop, servo lag, and a center of mass that won’t sit still, and just before you know it, the duck face plants into the floor. It took me 40+ calibration passes before it could take three steps without tipping! What the build came down to: • 3D-printed chassis • Per-joint offset calibration (where most of the pain lived) • Policy training in simulation (MuJoCo / Isaac Lab) • Build guide + docs via Tnkr • A lot of failed walks Real hardware. Real failures. Real progress.

Apr 12, 2026 You won’t believe your eyes, a real humanoid robot is out on the streets at night, running full speed and successfully herding a group of wild boars straight back into the forest. This is Edward Warchocki, a compact Unitree G1 humanoid robot standing about 132 cm tall. In this incredible clip, he charges behind a pack of “dziki”,  the wild boars that have become a serious urban problem across Poland. The animals scatter and bolt as the robot stays right on their heels, guiding them away from houses, gardens, and roads until they disappear into the treeline. Why is this happening? Wild boars have exploded in numbers in Polish towns and suburbs. With no natural predators left and plenty of easy food from trash bins, compost, and backyard gardens, they wander into residential areas every night. They root up lawns, damage property, knock over fences, and can become aggressive when surprised, creating real safety risks for families, pets, and drivers. Traditional solutions like hunting or fencing often fall short in crowded neighborhoods. That’s where Edward comes in. Instead of sending humans into potentially dangerous nighttime encounters, this innovative team is testing a non-lethal, high-tech solution: a fast, fearless robot that can patrol and scare the boars away safely and effectively. The footage shows it working perfectly,  the robot’s movement, lights, and presence are enough to make the boars turn tail and head back to the woods where they belong. This isn’t a movie scene or special effects. It’s actual, real world footage from a Polish town where wild boar invasions are a daily headache. Edward Warchocki, already famous for public appearances and his quirky personality, is now proving robots can handle practical problems in creative new ways. From dodging traffic to chasing boars, the future of everyday robotics is here, and it’s happening right now in Poland. Absolutely wild, totally real, and surprisingly effective.  Wild boars thought they owned the streets at night… until Edward showed up for his evening workout . When your robot takes night patrol duty, Edward Warchocki turning wild boars into speedy forest runners What’s the next fun job you’d give a humanoid robot like this one? #news #viral #CaughtOnCamera #fyp #ViralVideo

Wooden robots are a type of robot that are made from wood rather than metal or plastic. These robots often have a more organic and natural appearance, making them stand out from their more traditional counterparts. #wooden  robots can be used for a variety of purposes, from educational and research purposes to entertainment and art. Some wooden robots are even able to move and perform tasks, using a #combination of #traditional mechanical components and cutting-edge technology. Overall, wooden robots are a #unique and interesting alternative to traditional robots, offering a new perspective on the capabilities and potential of these incredible #machines.
